lane.name: FUSE91
lane.preregistration: docs/HYPOTHESES_F91.md (frozen before any F91 holdout number)

hypothesis: A supervised model that sees raw sponsor-band context, odd-symmetric cross-fault step responses, and depth-conditioned conductivity/curvature contacts together ranks concealed faults with higher kernel-credit density than any single view, because a buried normal fault steps topography, gravity, magnetics, basement depth and conductivity across strike even where it has no scarp and is therefore missing from the exposure-biased USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue.
mechanism: HistGradientBoosting (repo _train_hgb hyperparameters verbatim) on 52 features: 28 HGB-CTX (19 band percentiles + TRI3 percentile + 8 mean11 contexts) + 18 ASC antisymmetric step features (5 level fields x step magnitude/anisotropy/signed polarity + modal-azimuth agreement) + 6 new depth-conditioned features (conductivity residual vs continuous conditional median by depth-to-basement, its gradient/Laplacian, depth & gravity Laplacians, depth-gravity gradient collinearity). Winner E1 emission: greedy spaced unit dots, 2.8 px, 37,654 budget, >3 px off catalogue. No previous submission raster read as input, mask, ranking or prior; no distance-to-catalogue feature.
non_fault_mimic: Buried volcanic/intrusive lithologic margin (steps elevation, gravity, magnetics, basement depth and conductivity at the same place without being a Quaternary fault); saline-groundwater/clay conductivity contacts are the named mimic for the depth-conditioned subset.
